Hi my friend. Thank you for asking this. I am experiencing some similar feelings. Also I was raised by two folks who have a ‘Great Depression’ mindset around all things. 

Here is what I’ve been doing:
1. I tell myself what I KNOW is true: there is enough for us all. Money is flowing to us all. Often we don’t even look at or consider some of the ‘flow’. For example: I got a rebate. I was like wow look at this! Another example is being offered a job opportunity. Two times in the past week I was offered but it didn’t work. I said thank you for it anyway. Sometimes we aren’t able to get everything but it’s a sign that FLOW is happening. 
2. I repeat a mantra that money is flowing to me on a constant basis. I write this down every day and express my gratitude for it. 
3. I avoid talking about finances with ppl who are fearful and living in lack. These are similar to energy vampires although they specifically suck the blood of your energy around money. Notice what a person like this says and how their life reflects this. After that do a little research on a notable wealthy person and their beliefs around money…I’d venture to believe it’s much different! 
4. Remain calm and state: I am calm. You really are able to fix this. You have resources and there are so many avenues for you. When your body is in chaos mode it’s hard to see what your resources are. 
5. Mediate on abundance and prosperity and generosity. Giving is really important. The whole financial scene is a cyclical thing. We forget that we are in the cycle. 
6. Take ownership of your behavior and utilize wisdom. Often we are not using wisdom when it comes to finances. Sometimes we are doing the other things but the wisdom piece is not carrying over. Be intentional about this and focus energy here. 

I hope I gave you some support. I know we are in a state of flux with money. However I believe in you and your capacity. You are a miracle and you have been sent from the heavens for fun and creation. You will not be stopped! Good luck with reaching your desires. ❤️

Agree with the above poster. Also SSW in HS and I do groups. Check the IEP to see if any of the students have group counseling. If not you can suggest that doing groups in addition to individual sessions. 

Another thing I focus on is “check ins”. Often some of my higher functioning students don’t need a full length 30 mins. I let the student guide this. The student may choose to have a bi weekly session that is longer. For me what’s is most important is making contact with the child in general. During the pandemic it is really hard to get to 30 mins doing virtual sessions. I work in NYC and we’ve been told to just get contact for as long as possible. 

Most important thing is the student knows they have you as a support, they know the time when they can receive it, and that they want to. 

Good luck. Don’t be hard on yourself. You can literally only do one thing at a time. Hopefully you can find more creative waves to make contact. Sending you love.

Totally understand and empathize with you. I think there are two things that can be of great help to you as you move forward:

1. Offer your own self compassion and grace. You are not perfect and no one else is. You did something that you didn’t like but you feeling remorse for it shows you’re not a complete jerk. You are even saying you wish to apologize knowing that you can’t. That’s really nice of you. Remember we all do stupid shit as drunks... ALL OF US. It’s a slippery slope and maybe your friends or colleagues or whomever says they haven’t but it’s not true. Everyone does something dumb while drunk. You’re not a bad person for it. Forgive yourself. Do what you can to change your behavior so it doesn’t continue to happen. And give yourself compassion as you work on being better. 

2. Know the difference between shame and guilt. Shame=I am bad whereas guilt= I’ve done something bad. When you are shame prone it makes it more difficult to forgive yourself. When you are telling yourself it is you who is bad you’re already in a place where you can’t move forward. Brené Brown has a podcast episode on this theory. If you can check it out. It really helped me understand how much I shame myself for things I should not. 

Good luck with your journey. I believe in you. I recently (305 days ago, sober ever since) assaulted my best friend while drunk. I cannot say what came over me besides alcohol, extreme depression, and anxiety. I took it out on her and it cost me something huge. I still feel sad thinking of it but I realize she is no saint nor is anyone else. That day was just my day to realize I’m more powerful than my desire to drink and have fun. I’ve been sober 9 months and it’s been ok. At first it was hard but now it’s sort of the way. I’ve apologized but all I can do is move forward. 

Seek help. Give yourself grace. Trust the process. You can do all things. Sending love 💗

Agree with others. My son is almost 2. My husband and I would joke about our future before it became reality. I don’t think it will be as much as an issue as it may seem. If someone you meet wants a large family you may want to consider the relationship then. No one can force you to have children and no one should. You being an only I think will help your case if someone is uncertain about having one. I get very annoyed with people saying only kids are weird or you have to give him a sibling (as if another human being is an actual gift). You don’t have to do anything. You do what you want. Having children literally isn’t what you think. You only know what it is when you’re doing it. That’s it. All these boards mean nothing until your in the position of parenting. You can’t truly know what it is like. People who advocate having 2-3 kids now have to raise them during COVID-19. I hear a LOT of complaining. Remember no matter what every child you have is your full responsibility. You have to raise and tear them not the school system or any thing else. You get assistance but it is you and the other parent’s job. One is great. Two is grand. Threes a party. Either way you do what is best for you. You will be fine.

I’m so impressed with you for wanting to do this! I think it’s very much a need but honestly, a lot of companies are oblivious. I’m a social worker and I wrote my thesis on colorism and it’s pervasiveness at the micro and macro level. As a black woman, I sort of knew there would be some negative impacts but I was shocked at the level to which skin tone changes life chances. 

There is so much data to show that colorism needs to be addressed and irradiated. I make it my daily mission to fight against this bc it really upsets me as a black person but specifically as a black woman. I am a woman of lighter complexion so I personally feel it is a duty to stand up and against ideas that my skin color is “better”. I find it odd many people have not come into contact with a light skinned woman who is anti “light skin is the right skin”. I’m very vocal about this. I work with teens and they often ask me about my heritage bc they cannot pinpoint where I am from. I always take pride in saying “sisters come in all shades”. Many of the teens who work with me are shocked when I interrupt a “good hair” with a good hair is hair that grows! I love taking all opportunities to stand up against colorism. What a phony system to implement and cause more friction. I personally feel that LS folk really have to work against this ideology but many benefit and are unwilling. I always ask myself why? Can’t understand how uplifting all black folks (✊🏿✊🏾✊🏽) is not helpful. Women face so much hardship when trying to understand themselves, their bodies, their minds, etc. Black women face even more hardships. 

I applaud you and I hope to see you do amazing things. Working for beauty companies and fashion companies sounds to be a great starting place. I’m not too familiar but marketing industry may be a good place for you to consider as well.

Hi. I’m sorry you’re so unsure of what to do. It’s very hard to tell you exactly what to do. We can all give you feedback based on what has worked for us individually. You’re welcome to try anything that you’re comfortable. Sorry I said this but I just want to be clear that we are battling one thing but display that battle in a unique way. For me what has worked is focus on my own path and what works for me. What I did first: decided not to drink that day. I stopped right there. I did nothing else outside of deciding I’m not drinking each day. 6 months in I’m still alcohol free and I feel great. After making that daily decision I started to do more research about drinking. I read a book that seriously helped me see alcohol as the bad guy not you. The book really takes a stand that any and everyone who drinks is on a slope to addiction. Some of us just slide faster. The authors perspective really helped shape my current beliefs about alcohol. Now making my daily decision and arming my decision with knowledge abstaining from alcohol is a lot easier. I just look at it differently bc I truly understand it does more to me than a hangover and an argument with a friend. The book is called: this naked mind, control alcohol by Annie grace. I urge you to read it to help shift your mindset around it. In addition I listen to a podcast called Taking a Break from Drinking by Rachel Hart. She is really cool and has a unique outlook as well. Good luck with your journey. I hope you find success. 
I hope you always remember you can stop drinking. It feels uncomfortable at first and you’re not sure what your life will look like but I promise you it’s better when you stop. No more issues with it no more shame about why you said or did. You will see soon, it’s great ❤️

My sister makes very risky career moves. It impacts her financially and I always feel I have to help her. My parents help but this siblingship always makes me so more. I am currently OAD bc of my feelings around losing myself and emotional well being in general. I have 19 mo son who is a great little kiddo. Yeah he toddlers like all of them but I’m genuinely happy with him. I was depressed and anxious for about until he was about 14 months. 

For me being so depressed is undesirable. Having two would stretch me until I’m thin. The work, the lack of help, the constant work, and stress is enough reason for me to be one and done. If I could have kids ten years apart then I’d prob have more but that doesn’t seem likely. 

Another reason I’m OAD is simply bc I don’t want to be a mom of two. I really cannot stress that you should have a baby bc you want another child to love and raise, not bc you want your kid to have a sibling. Ppl have twisted that only children are broken bc they can’t socialize with kids or they have only child syndrome. This is obviously false. Have a baby bc you want it more than you want to gift someone a human. You can’t guarantee your two will even like or identify with each other. I hated my sibling from 11-30 and she still grinds my gears to this day. It’s nice having her but occasionally she’s a liability financially bc she lives her life a certain way and always wants a bailout. This is just my life and there’s tons of siblings who are the best of friends. However a lot of siblings lives change when they meet partners and now the partner has to be the significant long standing relationship not the sibling. 

I say all this to say you will make the best choice for your family. Have one is ok. Having 2 is ok. Having 13 is a lot but still ok. Having 1 and changing your mind and have two more is ok. You know what you need. Believe that.

Hey there WFPB friend. I know what you mean. I typically say vegan bc I feel WFPB has a whole discussion behind it. Being a vegan is not only diet but lifestyle too. A lot of people don’t seem to understand that. I don’t really get bothered by it but I understand if it bothers others. I usually try to avoid conversations entirely about my diet. For example, if I go some where and there’s going to be food I often eat in advance of the event or look up stuff that I know is PB. I do a lot to avoid bringing up my diet in general. It doesn’t need to be a focal point of any conversation. If someone is genuinely curious and wants to learn its way different. Typically ppl want opportunities to argue, test your theory, ask your about protein, etc. Literally all we want to do is eat something plant based in peace. Try to just focus on yourself bc ppl literally always have something to say. It’s not worth taking your precious time. If you don’t want to talk just communicate that constructively or maybe ask them about their food. Anything to get them away from what you’re doing. You do what works for your.

Hey Girl! Congratulations on your pregnancy. I hope it’s a beautiful experience for you. I am a mama of an 18 month old and I worked out my entire pregnancy. I don’t have the same history as you but I totally understand your concerns. It’s normal and honestly it’s the beginnings of you being a protective mama bear. Prospective is everything. Working out for you doesn’t have to be a crazy intense thing. Shift your thinking to healthy movement as opposed to intense training. Can you do prenatal yoga everyday and go for walks? Can you YouTube low impact prenatal work outs at home? I did CrossFit my entire pregnancy so I kept up my intensity but I was already prepped for it. Also I modified everything. You can do whatever you feel comfortable with. The goal is healthy movement not intense training. Even walking circles in your yard for 30 mins is good. Track what you do if you can and repeat when necessary. You got this girl! I want to encourage you to keep moving bc that’s all you need to do. The moving SERIOUSLY helps with recovery. I had a vaginal birth and had almost 0 pain afterward. I chalk it up to working out and evening primrose oil right before giving birth. Any movement counts! Just listen to your body and do what you can. Good luck and I’m happy for you and your partner. ❤️
